messages.author: b34b96b7ad286370
messages.subject: Enhanced Standard Analysis
parts: Dear QCA community, dear Adrian, I am currently working on a fsQCA in R using the QCA and the SetMethods packages and I encountered repeatedly an issue with the Enhanced Standard Analysis: Despite excluding contradictory assumptions for the most parsimonious solution and the intermediate solution, the excluded logical remainders (with OUT = 0 in the esa truth table) seem to be included in the enhanced parsimonious and the enhanced intermediate solution as simplifying assumptions or easy counterfactuals (at least they show up when I use "sol_y_pesa$SA" or "sol_ny_i$i.sol$C1P1$EC"). I don't quite understand this - shouldn't these logical remainders be excluded from the minimization in ESA?

messages.author: 53dbab5845ace6b6
messages.subject: Re: Enhanced Standard Analysis
parts:
Dear Anna,

It would likely be easier to follow with a minimal reproducible example (I find myself better at reading the R code behind the question).
Logical remainders do not have OUT = 0 in the truth table, but "?". True however, when remainders are excluded, they are indeed allocated a value of 0 in the truth table.

Did you use the argument "exclude" in the function truthTable(), or did you use the function esa() from package SetMethods?
I would recommend the first method, although I'm sure the function esa() is well tested.

Excluded remainders should not appear in the simplifying assumptions, that's for sure. That is why a reproducible example would make your question much easier to answer (I need to see this happening in order to assess what exactly is going on).

All the best,
Adrian

messages.author: a98c47479ea6b61f
messages.subject: Re: [QCA] Re: Enhanced Standard Analysis
parts:
Oh, I see what happens, there is nothing wrong with the function esa().
In Anna's code, at the minimization stage the argument n.cut is used, which makes no sense because the input in the minimization is already a truth table.

The argument n.cut is a formal argument from the function truthTable(), not from the function minimize().
It can be used but only when the input is the calibrated data, so that function minimize() calls truthTable() to internally construct the truth table.

In this case, by using the argument n.cut the function minimize() re-created the truth table (internally) overwriting the enhanced truth table created by function esa(), and that is how the previously excluded remainder 28 creeped in the solution.

It's a problem with the code, and with the approach. It had never occured to me this possibility might happen, and yet it is.
I did make this possible a few versions back, in order to re-create the truth table in function findRows(), possibly with different inclusion cut-offs and other parameters, for the negation of the outcome.

I'll try to think about a way to make this possibility a lot more difficult for end users, or perhaps issue some warnings this might happen so users can be alert.
So Anna, simply removing the argument n.cut from the call to function minimize(), should solve your problem.

I hope this explains it,
Adrian

messages.author: 53dbab5845ace6b6
messages.subject: Re: [QCA] Re: Enhanced Standard Analysis
parts:
As a second follow up, which might interest Carsten and Nena, this only happens when the function esa() is used, so it is indeed an issue with that function.
The reason is related to the way the function esa() modifies the truth table (by mechanically altering its rows) and I've long suspected this is potentially troublesome.

Irrespective of using the argument n.cut (or any other formal argument from the truth table command), the problem does not arise if the truth table is properly re-created using the formal argument "exclude".
(which is the reason why this problem has never surfaced in my hundreds of unit tests).

Using formal arguments from function truthTable() in function minimize() does trigger the modification of the truth table, according to its original call.
The new truth table, internally generated by the function minimize(), overwrites the truth table object from the input

In my case, the truth table gets modified but its structure remains the same, since in my call I've already used the "exclude = CSA" argument, for instance.
In the case of the truth table altered by esa(), the argument "exclude" was not part of the original call, therefore the modified truth table is different from the one produced by esa() which defeats the purpose.

Given these, I would naturally recommend Carsten and Nena to drop the function esa() altogether (but I know this is difficult).
It is more natural, and I would say a lot more clear, to re-create the truth table using the additional argument "exclude".

Perhaps I could even modify the truthTable() function to accept the original truth table object, so that instead of:

esa(oldtt = TT_y, contrad_rows = CSA)

one might do:

truthTable(TT_y, exclude = CSA)

I hope this helps, and further clarifies the situation,
Adrian
